_purpose: Sponsorship and TV/broadcast deals are the business-management layer of the sim, separate from match results. Teams choose which sponsorship tier to pursue; the league office (instructor) allocates TV revenue by a fixed formula. Money flows into each team's budget and can be spent on trades/free agents, but never raises the salary cap itself.
sponsorship_system: draft-and-negotiate, mandatory -- see engine/negotiation.py. Sponsors are organized into sponsorship_categories (Kit/Apparel, Beverage, Financial Services, Airline, Automotive, Technology), mirroring how a real club has exactly one jersey sponsor, one kit manufacturer, one official airline, etc. EVERY team must sign exactly one brand per category by the end of the Sponsorship Draft (sponsorship_categories_required in league_config.json) -- this is not optional. Multiple teams may hold the same brand (Nike sponsors many real clubs at once; qty is a league-wide cap on how many teams total, not an exclusivity lock). SPONSORS PAY TEAMS: there is no cost to sign -- season_revenue flows into the team, full stop, matching how real sponsorship deals work. In turn order (same shape as the player draft, cycling through all 6 categories), a team targets an available brand in whichever category they're filling and makes ONE ask (base / more_revenue / looser_clause, at Modest/Bold/Very Bold intensity), resolved instantly against the team's Negotiating Leverage. An unsuccessful bold ask means the sponsor walks -- the team simply tries a different brand in that same category, or accepts base terms elsewhere; a category can never go unfilled.

clause_enforcement.description: The performance clause is not flavor text -- it is a real revenue-at-risk condition, checked ONCE at the end of the season (the final round). Each clause level sets its OWN rank threshold the team must hit to keep the money -- a strict clause demands a genuinely strict standard (top 5), a loose clause only asks for an easy one (top 15). Miss your specific deal's threshold and that deal claws back a flat 20% of its revenue, regardless of which clause it was -- the clause you negotiated determines how HARD the bar is to clear, not how much you lose if you miss it. This is evaluated PER DEAL -- each sponsor AND a team's Local TV Deal alike, same table, same mechanic: a team holding a strict-clause sponsor, a loose-clause sponsor, and a standard-clause Local TV deal could clear two of those three bars while missing the third, and only lose money on the one it missed.
clause_enforcement.notes: Thresholds (top 5 / top 9 / top 14) are set for the current 18-team league -- roughly top 25% / 50% / 75% of the table -- rescale proportionally if team count changes. 'None' has no threshold and is never penalized, full stop. The penalty is a ONE-TIME 20% deduction from that specific sponsor's already-booked revenue, applied once at season end -- never applied twice to the same deal, and never applied at all to a deal that clears its threshold.

tv_deal_formula.description: League-wide broadcast revenue, paid once on TV Revenue Day together with each team's Local TV Deal. Modeled loosely on real sports-league media-rights revenue sharing: a shared base payment plus a performance bonus.
tv_deal_formula.standings_bonus: Top team on TV Revenue Day: +1,000,000. 2nd: +600,000. 3rd: +300,000. Everyone else: +0 (no penalty beyond missing the bonus).
tv_deal_formula.star_power_bonus: If a team's most recent starting-XI average Star Power ranks in the league's top 3 on TV Revenue Day, add +500,000 (broadcasters pay for star wattage independent of the standings). This can stack with the standings bonus.
tv_deal_formula.midseason_split_timing: One TV Revenue Day, once Local TV negotiations close. Your instructor announces the deadline. National and local money post to your budget together.

local_tv_deal_formula.description: A per-team regional broadcast contract, in addition to the league-wide national TV deal above, varying by market size. Each team signs it once, and it is fixed for the season.
local_tv_deal_formula.market_tiers: Every team is randomly assigned exactly one of five market tiers, split as evenly as possible across the league and drawn reproducibly from season_seed: Major Market (strict clause), Large Market (strict clause), Mid Market (standard clause), Small Market (standard clause), Micro Market (loose clause) -- higher-value markets carry a stricter clause, the same pattern Sponsorship's brand table uses. Your market tier's actual base rate is not publicly posted. The AI TV Rep opens with it when you sit down to negotiate, the same convention Sponsorship uses.
local_tv_deal_formula.star_power_modifier: If a team's most recent starting-XI average Star Power ranks in the league's top 3 on TV Revenue Day, its Local TV Deal pays +15% (the same top-3 test as the national star bonus), scaled off the team's own rate.
local_tv_deal_formula.payout_timing: Paid on TV Revenue Day together with the national deal. A team with no signed deal by the deadline is paid its market-tier base rate with its base clause.
local_tv_deal_formula.salary_cap_note: Local TV revenue flows into the team's budget like any other revenue; it never raises the salary cap itself.
local_tv_deal_formula.negotiation: Every team negotiates its Local TV Deal one-on-one with the AI TV Rep, under the same rules as the AI Sponsor Rep. The rep opens at your market tier's base rate and clause, and you can sign that straight away. Or negotiate: your Negotiating Leverage sets how far the network will go, from -10% to +10% of base, and a strong, data-backed pitch can add up to 2% within that limit. A weak hand can land below base. You get 6 offers, then a final offer. Asking far more than the network will pay is a strike, and after 3 strikes the rep walks away for the day. A looser clause is a separate ask: one step looser than base needs leverage 20+, two steps 50+, and strict to no clause 80+. AI-negotiated deals earn no commission. The clause is checked once at season end, with the same rank thresholds as a sponsorship clause. The manual form on the TV Rights page stays as a backup. On that form, a rate different from base credits the gap as a commission to the team that played the network rep, and a team cannot be its own rep.

playoffs.format: No bracket games are played. The top finishers in the final regular-season standings (see the qualification line marked on the dashboard, and the bonus table below) are recognized as Playoff Qualifiers -- a season-ending designation, not a separate elimination tournament.
playoffs.bonus_notes: Paid once, at season's end, to every team that finishes inside the qualification line -- not stacked or tiered by seed. 1st place and 6th place both earn this bonus equally; regular-season standings already reward finishing 1st over 6th through the Ranking component of the Season Scorecard.

trade_rules.deadline: There are two trade sessions this season. Trade Session 1 is open now and closes when Round 7 is simulated -- a trade must be accepted by both teams before then. Trade Session 2 will open later in the season; its date will be announced in class and on this page. Outside an open session, no trade can take effect -- this prevents last-minute roster stacking, the same reason real leagues carry a trade deadline.
trade_rules.player_limits: Each trade session, every team must move exactly 3 players out and bring exactly 3 players in -- no more, no less, so rosters always stay at 18. Incoming players can come from another team or from the free-agent pool (the undrafted players on the Draft Board). In any deal, the players you swap with a partner team must match one-for-one (1-for-1, 2-for-2 or 3-for-3). For each free agent you sign, you release one of your own players to the free-agent pool. Example: send 2 players to a partner for 2 of theirs, and release 1 player to sign 1 free agent. Your 3 can be one deal or several, but never more than 3 in a session. A partner in a 2-for-2 has only moved 2, so it still owes 1 more move that session.
trade_rules.voluntary: Trading is mandatory. By the end of each trade session every team must have moved its 3 players. You choose your partner and the terms, and nobody has to accept a particular offer -- if a deal isn't fair value, decline it and work out a better one, or use the free-agent pool instead. If two teams claim the same free agent, the lower-ranked team gets him (see Free-agent priority).
trade_rules.salary_cap: A trade is only valid if BOTH teams remain at or under salary_cap (see league_config.json) after the trade completes.
trade_rules.cash_considerations: Either side may add cash (from its budget, not a salary-cap item) on top of the player swap to make up for a value gap -- paying extra cash to land a clearly better player than what you're giving up is a normal, allowed trade structure, the same way real clubs attach cash to a deal. Cash only applies to deals with a partner team, not to free-agent moves.
trade_rules.approval: A deal with another team only takes effect once BOTH teams agree to it: the proposing team submits a Trade Proposal, and it sits pending until the receiving team accepts or declines it on the Trade Center page. Accepting applies it at the next league-office check (once it clears the roster/cap checks below); declining ends it with no changes to either roster. A free-agent-only move needs no one's approval, but like every free-agent signing it waits for waivers.
trade_rules.mid_season_trade_day: Each trade session includes an in-class Trade Day. Every owner must meet at least 3 other teams. Class starts with 3 short rotations: owners sit in two facing rows, meet one owner for 5 minutes, then rotate seats, so everyone meets 3 different teams. Use each meeting to find leads: what you would move, what positions you need, and your salary room. After the rotations, the room opens up: go back to your best leads or talk to any other team, agree on deals and submit them on this page before class ends. Your 3 players can be moved with any team or the free-agent pool, and the session stays open until it closes.
trade_rules.free_agent_priority: Free agents go to the lowest-ranked team first. Any deal that signs a free agent waits as a claim until the instructor processes waivers. Then every waiting claim is applied in reverse standings order, worst record first. If two teams claim the same free agent, the lower-ranked team gets him and the other claim is voided, so that team should submit a different move. Waiting claims are also processed right before the next round is simulated. Deals that don't involve free agents apply at the next league-office check as usual.
